meaningEn: to enter or to board a vehicle To get in is used for cars; to get on is used for all other forms of transportation.
examples: It's easiest to get in the car from the driver's side. The door on the other side doesn't work well.
I always get on the bus to work at 34th Street.

phrase: to get out of/to get off
meaningEn: to leave or to descend from a vehicle. To get out of is used for cars; to get off is used for all other forms of transportation.
examples: Why don't we stop and get out of the car for a while?
Helen got off the train at the 42nd Street terminal.

meaningEn: to place on oneself (usually said of clothes) (S)
examples: Mary put on her coat and left the room.
Put your hat on before you leave the house.

meaningEn: to remove (usually said of clothes) (S)
examples: John took off his jacket as he entered the office.
Take your sweater off. The room is very warm.

meaningEn: to telephone (also: to give some one a call) (S) To call can be used instead of to call up, as in the first example below.
examples: I forgot to call up Mr. Jones yesterday. I'd better call him now.
Call me up tomorrow, Jane. We'll arrange a time to have lunch together.
I promise to give you a call as soon as I arrive in New York.

meaningEn: to start or cause to function (also: to switch on) (S)
examples: Please turn on the light; it's too dark in here.
Do you know who turned the air conditioning on?

meaningEn: to cause to stop functioning (also: to switch off, to shut off) (S) Turn on and turn off, as well as their related forms, are used for things that flow, such as electricity, water, gas, etc.
examples: Please turn off the light when you leave the room.
Are you really listening to the radio, or should I turn it off?

meaningEn: very soon; immediately (also: at once)
examples: Dad says that dinner will be ready right away, so we'd better wash our hands and set the table.
Tell Will to come to my office right away. I must see him immediately.
Stop playing that loud music at once!

meaningZh: 拾起，購員，搭載某人(搭便
meaningEn: to lift form the floor, table, etc., with one's fingers (S)
examples: Harry picked up the newspaper that was on the front doorstep.
Could you pick your toy up before someone falls over it?

meaningEn: eventually, after a period of time
examples: If you study English seriously, sooner or later you'll become fluent.
I'm too tired to do my homework now; I'm sure I'll do it sooner or later.

meaningEn: to arise, to rise from a bed; to make someone arise (S) For the last definition a noun phrase must separate the verb and particle.
examples: Carla gets up at seven o'clock every morning.
At what time should we get the children up tomorrow?

meaningEn: in the beginning, originally
examples: At first English was difficult for him, but later he made great progress.
I thought at first that it was Sheila calling, but then I realized that it was Betty.

meaningEn: to wear formal clothes, to dress very nicely
examples: We should definitely dress up to go to the theater.
You don't have to dress up for Mike's party.

meaningEn: finally, after a long time.
examples: We waited for hours and then the train arrived at last.
Now that I am sixteen, at last I can drive my parents' car.

meaningEn: as is the general case, as is typical
examples: George is late for class as usual. This seems to happen every day.
As usual, Dora received first prize in the swimming contest. It's the third consecutive year that she has won.

meaningEn: get information about, to determine (S) This idiom is separable only when a pronoun is used, as in the second example.
examples: Will you please try to find out what time the airplane arrives?
I'll call right now to find it out.

meaningEn: give one's attention to; to watch
examples: The teacher told us to look at the blackboard and not at our books.
I like to walk along a country road at night and look at the stars.

meaningEn: to try to find, to search for An adverb phrase such as all over can be put between the verb and preposition, as in the second example, however, the idiom cannot be separated by a noun or pronoun.
examples: He's spent over an hour looking for the pen that he lost.
So there you are! We've looked allover for you.

meaningEn: acceptable, fine; yes, okay This idiom can also be spelled alright in informal usage.
examples: He said that it would be all right to wait in her office until she returned.
Do you want me to turn off the TV? Alright, if you insist.

meaningEn: all the time, from the beginning (without change)
examples: She knew all along that we'd never agree with his plan.
You're smiling! Did you know all along that I'd give you a birthday present?

meaningEn: gradually, slowly (also: step by step)
examples: Karen's health seems to be improving little by little.
If you study regularly each day, step by step your vocabulary will increase.

meaningEn: to make very weary due to difficult conditions or hard effort (also: to wear out) (S)
examples: The hot weather tired out the runners in the marathon.
Does studying for final exams wear you out? It makes me feel worn out!

meaningEn: to ask for a response from; to visit (also: to drop in on)
examples: Jose didn't know the answer when the teacher called on him.
Last night several friends called on us at our home.
Shy don't we drop in on Sally a little later?

meaningEn: don't be concerned about it; ignore what was just said
examples: When he spilled his drink on my coat, I said, "Never mind. It needs to be cleaned anyway."
So you weren't listening to me again. Never mind; it wasn't important.

meaningEn: to choose, to select (S)
examples: Ann picked out a good book to give to her brother as a graduation gift.
Johnny, if you want me to buy you a toy, then pick one out now.

meaningEn: to do without rush, not to hurry This idiom is often used in the imperative form. (See the first example)
examples: There's no need to hurry doing those exercises. Take your time.
William never works rapidly. He always takes his time in every thing that he does.

meaningEn: to discuss or consider a situation with others (S)
examples: We talked over Carla's plan to install an air conditioner in the room, but we couldn't reach a decision.
Before I accepted the new job offer, I talked the matter over with my life.

meaningEn: to place oneself in a flat position, to recline
examples: If you are tired, why don't you lie down for an hour or so?
The doctor says that Grace must lie down and rest for a short time every afternoon.

meaningEn: to rise from a sitting or lying position (also: to get up)
examples: When the president entered the room, everyone stood up.
Suzy, stop rolling around on the floor; get up now.

meaningEn: to be seated (also: take a seat)
examples: We sat down on the park bench and watched the children play.
There aren't any more chairs, but you can take a seat on the floor.

meaningEn: the entire day, week, month, year
examples: I've been working on my income tax forms all day long. I've hardly had time to eat.
It's been raining all week long. We haven't seen the sun since last Monday.

meaningEn: alone, without assistance
examples: Francis translated that French novel by himself. No one helped him.
Paula likes to walk through the woods by herself, but her brother prefers to walk with a companion.

meaningEn: for a reason, deliberately This idiom is usually used when someone does something wrong or unfair.
examples: Do you think that she didn't come to the meeting on purpose?
It was no accident that he broke my glasses. He did it on purpose.

meaningEn: to associate or work well with; to succeed or manage in
examples: Terry isn't getting along with her new roommate; they argue constantly.
How are you getting on with your students?

meaningEn: to be of importance (to), to affect This idiom is often used with adjectives to show the degree of importance.
examples: It makes a big difference to me whether he likes the food I serve.
Does it make any difference to you where we go for dinner?
No, it doesn't make any difference.

meaningEn: to remove, to extract (S); to go on a date with (S) (also to go out with)
examples: Student, take out your books and open them to page twelve.
Did you take Sue out last night?
No, she couldn't go out with me.

meaningEn: to be involved in, to participate in (also: to be in on)
examples: Martin was sick and could not take part in the meeting yesterday.
I didn't want to be in on their argument, so I remained silent.

meaningEn: to any degree (also: in the least)
examples: Larry isn't at all shy about expressing his opinions.
When I asked Donna whether she was tired, she said, "Not in the least. I'm full of energy."

meaningEn: to locate information in a directory, dictionary, book, etc. (S)
examples: Ellen suggested that we look up Lee's telephone number in the directory.
Students should try to understand the meaning of a new word from context before looking the word up in the dictionary.

meaningEn: to serve in a store or restaurant
examples: A very pleasant young clerk waited on me in that shop.
The restaurant waitress asked us, "Has anyone waited on you yet?

meaningEn: a minimum of, no fewer (or less) than
examples: I spend at least two hours every night on my studies.
Mike claims that he drinks at least a quart of water every day.

meaningEn: until now, until the present time (also: up to now, as of yet) This idiom is usually used with the present perfect tense.
examples: So far, this year has been excellent for business. I hope that the good luck continues.
How many idioms have we studied in this book up to now?
As of yet, we have not had an answer from him.

phrase: to take a walk, stroll, hike, etc.
meaningEn: to go for a walk, stroll, hike, etc. A stroll involves slow, easy walking; a hike involves serious, strenuous walking.
examples: Last evening we took a walk around the park.
It's a fine day. Would you like to take a stroll along Mason Boulevard?
Let's take a hike up Cowles Mountain this afternoon.

meaningEn: to go on a journey, to travel
examples: I'm so busy at work that I have no time to take a trip.
During the summer holidays, the Thompsons took a trip to Europe.

meaningEn: to wear clothes to check the style or fit before buying (S)
examples: He tried on several suits before he picked out a blue one.
Why don't you try these shoes on next?

meaningEn: to consider carefully before deciding (S)
examples: I'd like to think over your offer first. Then can we talk it over tomorrow?
You don't have to give me your decision now. Think it over for a while.

meaningEn: to occur, to happen according to plan
examples: The regular meetings of the committee take place in Constitution Hall.
I thought that the celebration was taking place at John's house.

meaningEn: to remove from slight, to put in the proper place (S)
examples: Please put away your papers before you open the test booklet.
John put the notepad away in his desk when he was finished with it.

meaningEn: to be careful or cautious (also: to watch out) Both of these idioms can occur with the preposition for.
examples: "Look out!" Jeffrey cried as his friend almost stepped in a big hole in the ground.
Look out for reckless drivers whenever you cross the street.
Small children should always watch out for strangers offering candy.

meaningEn: to exchange greetings by clasping hands
examples: When people meet for the first time, they usually shake hands.
The student warmly shook hands with his old professor.

meaningEn: to return (S)
examples: Mr. Harris got back from his business trip to Chicago this morning.
Could you get the children back home by five o'clock?

meaningEn: to become sick with a cold of the nose for throat
examples: If you go out in this rain, you will surely catch cold.
How did she ever catch cold in such warm weather?

meaningEn: to recover from an illness; to accept a loss or sorrow
examples: It took me over a month to get over my cold, but I'm finally well now.
It seems that Mr. Mason will never get over the death of his wife.

meaningEn: to reach a decision, to decide finally
examples: Sally is considering several colleges to attend, but she hasn't made up her mind yet.
When are you going to make up your mind about your vacation plans?

meaningEn: to alter one's decision or opinion
examples: We have changed our minds and are going to Canada instead of California this summer.
Matthew has changed his mind several times about buying a new cat.

meaningEn: temporarily (also: for now)
examples: For the time being, Janet is working as a waitress, but she really hopes to become an actress soon.
We're living in an apartment for now, but soon we'll be looking for a house to buy.

meaningEn: permanently, forever
examples: Ruth has returned to Canada for good. She won't ever live in the United States again.
Are you finished with school for good, or will you continue your studies some day?

meaningEn: to cancel (S)
examples: The referee called off the soccer game because of the darkness.
The president called the meeting off because she had to leave town.

meaningEn: to postpone (S)
examples: Many student's put off doing their assignments until the last minute.
Let's put the party off until next weekend, okay?

meaningEn: hurried, rushed (also: in a rush)
examples: Alex seems in a hurry; he must be late for his train again.
She's always in a rush in the morning to get the kids to school.

meaningEn: not feeling well, sick
examples: John stayed home from work because he was feeling under the weather.
When you cat cold, you feel under the weather.

meaningEn: to place clothes on a hook or hanger (S); to replace the receiver on the phone at the end of a conversation (S)
examples: Would you like me to hang up your coat for you in the closet?
The operator told me to hang the phone up and call the number again.

meaningEn: to trust someone in time of need (also: to depend on)
examples: I can count on my parents to help me in an emergency.
Don't depend on Frank to lend you any money; he doesn't have any.

meaningEn: to become friendly with others
examples: Patricia is a shy girl and doesn't make friends easily.
During the cruise Ronald made friends with almost everyone on the ship.

meaningEn: not in working condition
examples: The elevator was out or order, so we had to walk to the tenth floor of the building.
We couldn't use the soft drink machine because it was out of order.

meaningEn: to be able to do something special; to arrive at a place, such as home, work, etc. for the second definition, do not use the preposition to with the words home or there.
examples: The children got to stay up late and watch a good movie for the family.
I missed the bus and couldn't get to the office until ten o'clock.
When are you planning to get home tonight?

meaningEn: not frequent, unusual, rare
examples: The times that our children get to stay up late are few and far between.
Airplane travel is very safe because accidents are few and far between.

meaningEn: to examine, to inspect closely (also: to go over, to read over, to check over) (S) Go over is different from the other forms because it is not separable.
examples: I want to look my homework over again before I give it to the teacher.
The politician went over his speech before the important presentation.
You should never sign any legal paper without checking it over first.

meaningEn: to have free time, not to have to work (also: to take time off (S)) The related form (S) to take time off is used when someone makes a decision to have free time, sometimes when others might not agree with the decision.
examples: Every morning the company workers have time off for a coffee break.
Several workers took the afternoon off to go to a baseball game.

meaningEn: to happen; to resume, to continue (also: to keep on)
examples: Many people gathered near the accident to see what was going on.
I didn't mean to interrupt you. Please go on.
The speaker kept on talking even though most of the audience had left.

meaningEn: extinguish, to cause to stop functioning (S) To put out has the same meaning as to turn off (Lesson 1) for a light fixture.
examples: No smoking is allowed in here. Please put out your cigarette.
The fire fighters worked hard to put the brush fire out.
Please put out the light before you leave. Okay, I'll put it out.

meaningEn: suddenly, without warning (also: all at once)
examples: All of a sudden Ed appeared at the door. We weren't expecting him to drop by.
All at once Millie got up and left the house without any explanation.

meaningEn: to show, to indicate, to bring to one's attention (S)
examples: What important buildings did the tour guide point out to you?
The teacher pointed out the mistakes in my composition.
A friend pointed the famous actor out to me.

meaningEn: to expire, to be finished This idiom is used only with the word time as the subject.
examples: "The time is up," the teacher said at the end of the test period.
We have to leave the tennis court because our hour is up; some other people want to use it now.

meaningEn: to be finished, to end (also: to be through) This idiom is used for activities and events.
examples: After the dance was over, we all went to a restaurant.
The meeting was through ten minutes earlier than everyone expected.

meaningEn: exactly at the correct time, punctually
examples: I thought that Margaret would arrive late, but she was right on time.
Did you get to work on time this morning, or did rush hour traffic delay you?

meaningEn: before the time necessary to do something
examples: We entered the theater just in time to see the beginning of the movie.
The truck was not able to stop in time to prevent an accident.

meaningEn: to become better, worse, etc.
examples: Heather has been sick for a month, but now she is getting better.
This medicine isn't helping me. Instead of getting better, I'm getting worse.

phrase: to get sick, well, tired, busy, wet, etc.
meaningEn: to become sick, well, tired, busy, wet, etc. This idiom consists of a combination of get and various adjectives.
examples: Gerald got sick last week and has been in bed since that time.
Every afternoon I get very hungry, so I eat a snack.

meaningEn: should, ought to, be advisable to This idiom is most often used in contracted form (I'd better).
examples: I think you'd better speak to Mr. White right away about this matter.
The doctor told the patient that he'd better go home and rest.

meaningEn: prefer to (also: would just as soon)
examples: Would you rather have the appointment this Friday or next Monday?
I would just as soon go for a walk as watch TV right now.

meaningEn: to stop working for the rest of the day/night
examples: Herb tried to repair his car engine all morning before he called it a day and went fishing.
We've been working hard on this project all evening; let's call it a night.

meaningZh: 想念，作 ~ 看法，對 ~ 認
meaningEn: to have a (good or bad) opinion of This idiom is often used in the negative or with adjectives such as much and highly.
examples: I don't think much of him as a baseball player; he's a slow runner and a poor hitter.
James thinks highly of his new boss, who is a kind and helpful person.

meaningEn: to be at the moment of doing something, to be ready This idiom is often sued with the adverb just.
examples: I was just about to leave when you telephoned.
Oh, hi, John. We're just about to eat dinner.

meaningEn: to move or face in the opposite direction (S); to completely change the condition of (S)
examples: The man turned his car around and drove back the way he came.
The company has been very successful since the new business manager was able to turn it around.

meaningEn: to alternate, to change people while doing something
examples: During the trip, Darlene and I took turns driving so that neither of us would tire out.
I have to make sure that my two sons take turns playing the video game.

meaningEn: to look at and listen to someone while they are speaking, to concentrate
examples: Please pay attention to me while I'm speaking to you!
You'll have to pay more attention in class if you want to get a good grade.

meaningEn: to review something in order to refresh one's memory
examples: Before I traveled to Mexico, I brushed up on my Spanish; I haven't practiced it since high school.
In order to take that advanced mathematics class, Sidney will have to brush up on his algebra.

meaningEn: repeatedly (also: time after time, time and again)
examples: The actress studied her lines in the movie over and over until she knew them well.
Children have difficulty remembering rules, so it's often necessary to repeat them over and over again.
Time and again I have to remind Bobby to put on his seatbelt in the car.

meaningEn: to use something until it has no value or worth anymore, to make useless through wear (S)
examples: When I wear out these shoes, I'll have to buy some that last longer.
What do you do with your clothes after your wear them out?

meaningEn: to discard, to dispose of (S)
examples: I generally throw away my clothes when I wear them out.
Don't throw the magazines away; I haven't read them yet.

meaningEn: to begin to love This idiom is used with the expression at first sight to indicate a sudden interest in love.
examples: Ben and Sal fell in love in high school, and got married after graduation.
Have you ever fallen in love at first sight?

meaningEn: to stop functioning; to stop burning; to leave home or work (also: to step out)
examples: The lights went out all over the city because of an electrical problem.
The campers didn't have to put out the fire because it went out by itself.
Gary isn't here right now; he went out to the store for a moment.

meaningEn: impossible, not feasible
examples: Stephen told Deborah that it was out of the question for her to borrow his new car.
Don't expect me to do that again. It's absolutely out of the question.

meaningEn: to have some connection with or relationship to
examples: Ralph insisted that he had nothing to do with breaking the window.
What does your suggestion have to do with our problem?

meaningEn: to arise from sleep, to awaken (S) Compare wake up and get up (Lesson 1) as used in the first example.
examples: Marge woke up this morning very early, but she did not get up until about ten o'clock.
My alarm clock wakes me up at the same time every day.

meaningEn: to manage, to have responsibility for
examples: Jane is in charge of the office while Mrs. Haig is a business trip.
Who is in charge of arrangements for the dance next week?

meaningEn: just after, when
examples: As soon as it started to snow, the children ran outside with big smiles on their faces.
I'm busy now, but I'll meet you as soon as I've finished this work.

meaningEn: to communicate with, to contact
examples: You can get in touch with him by calling the Burma Hotel.
I've been trying all morning to get in touch with Miss Peters, but her phone is always busy.

meaningEn: to enjoy oneself
examples: We all had a good time at the class reunion last night.
Did you have a good time at the park? I really enjoyed it.

meaningEn: very quickly, rapidly This idiom can be used with the idiom at all to add emphasis to the certainty of the statement.
examples: Mac said that he'd be ready to leave in no time.
We thought that the meeting would take two hours, but it was over in no time at all.

meaningEn: to reduce, to lessen (also: to cut back on)
examples: In order to lose weight, you have to cut down on your intake of sugar.
The doctor told me to cut back on exercise until my back injury heals.

meaningEn: many
examples: Quite a few students were absent yesterday; in fact, more than half of them were not there.
We did not expect many people to attend to affair, but quite a few of our friends actually came.

meaningEn: formerly did, had the habit of This idiom is used to indicate a past situation, action, or habit that does not exist in the present. The idiom is always followed by a simple verb form.
examples: I used to live in New York, but I moved to California two years ago.
Kim used to smoke cigarettes, but she stopped the habit last month.

meaningEn: be accustomed to This idiom refers to a situation, action, or habit that continues in the present. The idiom is always followed by a noun or gerund phrase.
examples: He is used to this climate now, so the changes in temperature do not affect him much.
I am used to studying in the library, so it's difficult for me to study at home now.

meaningEn: to become used to, to become adjusted to This idiom describes the process of change that allows someone to be used to a situation, action, or habit.
examples: It took Yoshiko a long time to get used to the food that her American host family served her.
Mark can't seem to get used to wearing contact lenses; recently he's been wearing his glasses a lot.

meaningEn: in a backward and forward motion
examples: The restless lion kept pacing back and forth along the front of its cage.
Grandmother finds it relaxing to sit in her rocking chair and move back and forth.

meaningEn: to be sure, to ascertain (also: to make certain)
examples: Please make sure that you turn off the radio before you go out.
Could you make certain of the time? I don't want to miss that TV show.

meaningEn: occasionally, sometimes (also: now and again, at times, from time to time, off and on, once in a while) Both now and then and once in a while can be preceded by the adjective every. Another idiom with the same meaning and form is every so often.
examples: I don't see him very often, but (every) now and then we arrange to have lunch together.
Gary gets a cold (every) once in a while even though he takes good care of himself.
Every so often my brother and I get together for a camping trip.

meaningEn: to eliminate, to remove; to discard, to throw away
examples: Jerry tried hard to get rid of the stain on his shirt, but he never succeeded.
The stain was so bad that Jerry finally had to get rid of his shirt.

meaningEn: every second (one), alternate (ones)
examples: I play tennis with my father every other Saturday, so I usually play twice a month.
There were twenty problems in the exercise, but the teacher told us only to do every other one. Actually, doing ten problems was difficult enough.

meaningEn: to match, to compare well in color to design; to date, to
examples: That striped shirt goes well with the gray pants, but the pants go poorly with those leather shoes.
Eda went with Richard for about six months, but now she is going out with a new boyfriend.

meaningEn: excellent, superb
examples: The food served in that four-star restaurant is truly first-rate.
The Beverly Hills Hotel provides first-rate service to its guests.

meaningEn: to originate from This idiom is commonly used in discussion of one's home town, state, or country.
examples: What country in South American does she come from? She comes from Peru.
I just learned that he really comes from Florida, not Texas.
Where did this package come from? The mail carrier brought it.

meaningEn: to travel a sufficient distance at a reasonable speed The adjective excellent can also be used.
examples: On our last trip, it rained the entire time, so we didn't make good time.
We made excellent time on our trip to Florida; it only took eighteen hours.

meaningEn: to stir or shake well (S); to confuse, to bewilder (S) For the second definition, the passive forms to be mixed up or to get mixed up are often used.
examples: You should mix up the ingredients well before you put them in the pan.
The teacher's poor explanation really mixed the students up.
The students think it's their fault that they are mixed up so often.

meaningEn: to give attention or time to (also: to attend to, to see to)
examples: Who is going to see about getting us a larger room for the meeting?
I'll see to arranging music for the wedding of you attend to the entertainment.

meaningEn: to do, to succeed, to progress
examples: Charlie didn't make out very well on his final examinations. He may have to repeat one or more classes.
How did Rachelle make out on her acting audition in Hollywood yesterday?

meaningEn: by memorizing
examples: He knows many passages form Shakespeare by heart.
Do you know all the idioms you have studied in this book by heart?

meaningEn: not to enter, not allow to enter (S)
examples: There was a large sign outside the door that said, "Danger! Keep out!"
I've told you to keep the dog out of the house.

meaningEn: to stay at a distance (from) (S); to avoid use of (also: stay away from)
examples: Please be sure to keep the children away from the street!
The signs on the burned-out house said, "Keep Away! Danger Zone."
It's important for your health to stay away from dangerous drugs.

meaningEn: criticize, to complain about something
examples: It is very easy to find fault with the work of others, but more difficult to accept criticism of one's own work.
Mrs. Johnson is always finding fault with her children, but they really try to please their mother.

meaningEn: to be responsible for deciding; to be doing as a regular activity The second definition is most often used in a question as a form of greeting.
examples: I don't care whether we go to the reception or not. It's up to you.
Hi, George. I haven't seen you in a while. What have you been up to?

meaningEn: uncomfortable or worried in a situation
examples: Speaking in front of a large audience makes many people feel ill at ease.
My wife and I were ill at ease because our daughter was late coming home from a date.

meaningEn: to revise, to do again (S) A noun or pronoun must separate the two parts of this idiom.
examples: You'd better do the letter over because it is written so poorly.
Jose made so many mistakes in his homework that the teacher made him do it over.

meaningEn: to investigate, to examine carefully (also: to check into)
examples: The police are looking into the matter of the stolen computers.
The congressional committee will check into the financial dealings of the government contractor.

meaningEn: to grasp, to grip with the heads
examples: You should take hold of the railing as you go down those steep stairs.
The blind man took hold of my arm as I led him across the street.

meaningEn: to finish, to complete This idiom is followed either by the –ing form of a verb (a gerund) or by the preposition with.
examples: I didn't get through studying last night until almost eleven o'clock.
At what time does your wife get through with work every day?

meaningEn: from this time into the future
examples: Mr. Lee's doctor told him to cut down on eating fatty foods from now on, or else he might suffer heart disease.
I'm sorry that I dropped by at a bad time. From now on I'll call you first.

meaningEn: to keep or maintain a record of; to remember the location of
examples: Steve keeps track of all the long-distance telephone calls related to his business that he makes from his house.
With seven small children, how do the Wilsons keep track of all of them?

meaningEn: to be greatly affected by a strong feeling (S) This idiom can also be used with get instead of be.
examples: Paula and Leanne were carried away by the sad movie that they saw together.
James got carried away with anger when his roommate crashed his new car into a telephone pole.

meaningEn: modern; current, timely Hyphens (-) separate the parts of this idiom when it precedes a noun form, as in the third example. The verb to update derives from this idiom.
examples: The president insisted that the company bring its aging equipment up to date.
This catalog is not up to date. It was published several years ago.
The news program gave an up-to-date account of the nuclear accident. The newscaster said that he would update the news report every half hour.

The economies of some nations are worse off than they were several decades ago.

meaningEn: to have enough money to enjoy a comfortable life, to be rich (also: to be well-to-do)
examples: They live in the best section of town in a large home; they are very well- off.
By the time I reach the age of fifty-five, I hope to be well-to-do and to travel frequently.

meaningEn: to surprise, to amaze, to astonish (S) A noun or pronoun usually divides this idiom.

examples: You can telephone me every few days, and in that way we can keep in touch with each other.
He promised to stay in touch with us while he was abroad. However, we were very disappointed that he never did get in touch with us.

meaningEn: to give the same name as another (S)
examples: Helen's parents named Helen after her grandmother.
My grandson is named after Calvin Coolidge, the 30th President of the United States.

meaningEn: to grasp tightly or firmly; to wait, to be patient The second definition is often used when someone is talking on the telephone.
examples: The little girl held on to her mother's hand and refused to let go as they walked through the large crowd of people.
(on the telephone) Could you please hold on a moment while I get a pencil and paper?
Come on, Mike, hold on. I can't get ready so quickly.

meaningEn: to visit or stop somewhere briefly in order to do something
examples: James had to stop by the registrar's office to submit a transcript request form.
Let's stop by the supermarket and pick up a few grocery items.

meaningEn: to write a note to someone (S)
examples: As soon as I get to Florida, I'll drop you a line and tell you about my new job.
If you have time, drop me a line now and then while you're traveling.

meaningEn: to meet or find unexpectedly (also: to run across); to be
examples: While Cheryl was cleaning the attic, she came across some very old coins. It took her by surprise to run across something like that.
Jeff's boss comes across as a tough, unpleasant person, but actually Jeff says that he is a good employer.
Some people come off quite differently than they really are.

meaningEn: to represent, to signify; to tolerate The second definition is usually used in a negative sense. The meaning is the same as to put up with in Lesson 19.

The citizens wouldn't stand for the increase in crime in their city, so they hired more police officers and built another jail.

meaningEn: to have the possibility of accomplishing something This idiom is often used with an adjective such as good or excellent. It also occurs in the negative, sometimes with the adjective much.
examples: The New York baseball team stands a good chance of winning the World Series this year.

The woman injured in the serious train accident doesn't stand much chance of surviving.

meaningEn: to work carefully and conscientiously
examples: She takes pains to do everything well; she's our best employee.
He took great pains with his last assignment because he needed to get an excellent grade to pass the class.

meaningEn: to watch as a spectator, to observe
examples: Hundreds of people were looking on as the police and firefighters rescued the passengers in the wrecked train.
I stayed with my son at his first soccer practice and looked on as the coach worked with the boys.

meaningEn: to admire, to respect greatly
examples: Children will most certainly look up to their parents if the children are brought up well.
Everyone looks up to the director of our department because he is a kind and generous person.

meaningEn: to feel superior to, to think of someone as less important
examples: People who are in positions of power should be careful not to look down on those who work for them.
Why does Alma look down on Mario just because his family is so poor?

meaningEn: to leave the ground (for airplanes); to leave, often in a hurry The noun form takeoff derives from this idiom.
examples: The plane took off over an hour late. The passengers had to buckle their seatbelts during takeoff.
Do you have to take off already? You just arrive an hour ago!

meaningEn: to succeed in doing something difficult (S); to exit to the side of a highway
examples: The group of investors pulled off a big deal by buying half the stock in that company. I wonder how they pulled it off before the company could prevent it.
The motorist pulled off when the police officer turned on the red lights and the siren.

meaningEn: to operate accurately (for watches and clocks) This idiom is usually used with adjectives such as good and perfect.
examples: Although this is a cheap watch, it keeps good time.
The old clock keeps perfect time; it's never fast or slow.

meaningEn: to manage, to cope This idiom is used when a person must accept a substitute that is not the most suitable.
examples: Pearl doesn't have a clean blouse so she has to make do with the one she wore yesterday.
During difficult economic times, many people have to make do with less.

meaningEn: to bear a human being or animal
examples: Jane's mother has just given birth to twin girls.
The zoo's Siberian tiger just gave birth to a baby cub.

meaningEn: a situation involving a narrow escape from danger (also: close shave)
examples: Bob, that car nearly hit us! What a close call.
We had a close call when a small fire in our kitchen almost spread to the rest of the house.

meaningEn: to annoy or disturb (also: to bug)
examples: Laura loves to talk to anyone. Sometimes her chatter really gets on my nerves.
Jack asked his neighbor to turn down the stereo because it was bugging him and he couldn't concentrate.

meaningEn: to suppress, to quell (S); to criticize unfairly (S)
examples: The police arrived just in time to put down the disturbance before it got very serious.
Fred tries his best at playing tennis. You shouldn't put him down like that.

meaningEn: to be sold at a certain price; to seek or strive for
examples: This dress probably goes for about $50, don't you think?
Peter was going for first place in the swim meet, but he wasn't able to do better than third place.

meaningEn: to have as an interest, such as a sport or hobby (also: to go for, to be into, to get into)
examples: Hal goes in for tennis while his wife goes for painting and sculpture.
What sports are you into? I don't have any time to get into sports.

meaningEn: to remain awake, not to go to bed
examples: I want to stay up tonight and watch a late movie on TV.
He stays up every night until after one o'clock, preparing his homework.

meaningEn: to remain at home, not to go out An idiom with the opposite meaning is to stay out.
examples: On a rainy day, I like to stay in and read.
Young people are able to stay out late at night and get very little sleep.

meaningEn: to assume control or responsibility for (S); to do or perform again (S) The meaning of the second definition is almost the same as do over in Lesson 11. also for the second definition, a noun or pronoun must divide the idiom.

Most students didn't do well on the important test, so the instructor let them take it over.
Little Mickey didn't have much chance to hit the baseball during practice, so the coach let him take his turn over.

meaningEn: to appear, to arrive; to be found or located (also for the second
examples: It really gets on my nerves that Ursula shows up late for every meeting.

We've looked everywhere for that book, but it hasn't turned up yet.

meaningEn: to empty, to tidy by removing (S); to steal, to rob (S); to buy or purchase all of something (S)
examples: It's time for you to clean out your closet so that you can store more things in there.
A burglar entered my apartment while I was gone and cleaned me out. He took over $200 in cash and jewelry.
Thousands of shoppers cleaned out the store that had gone bankrupt and was selling all its remaining products at very reduced prices.

meaningEn: to make unconscious (S); to impress or attract greatly (S) This idiom can be made into the noun form knockout for both definitions.

examples: She really knocked herself out trying to pass that difficult class.

meaningEn: to accomplish, to execute (S) (also: to go through with)
examples: It's easy to write down a plan for losing weight, but much harder to carry it out.
Charles promised to go through with his plan to enroll in graduate school and get an advanced degree.

meaningEn: to meet someone unexpectedly; to crash or collide into (also: to bump into)
examples: It was a shock to run into an old friend from high school recently.
The drunk driver was slightly injured when he ran into a telephone pole.

meaningEn: to start traveling toward a place (also: to set off, to heat out); to

meaningEn: to create by drawing, such as a map (S); to prepare documents or legal papers (S)
examples: Max asked me to draw up a map to the party so that he wouldn't get lost.
Our lawyer agreed to draw the contract up as soon as possible.

meaningEn: compromise, cooperation between people
examples: Give and take is an important element of a successful marriage.
Most business negotiations involve give and take between the parties involved.

meaningEn: to stop attending; to withdraw from This idiom can be made into the noun form dropout.
examples: Some students drop out of secondary school early in order to get jobs. However, such dropouts often regret their decision later in life.
Two more baseball teams have dropped out of the youth league due to a lack of players.

meaningEn: to accept as true, have faith in
examples: Some people believe in being honest in all human affairs, while others accept the need to lie in order to get one's way.
Throughout the history of man, some cultures have believed in one god while others have believed in the existence of many gods.

meaningEn: to make happier, to feel less sad (S)
examples: We all tried to cheer up the little boy when he stared to cry.
After the death of Deanne's husband, it was difficult to cheer her up at all.

meaningEn: to be sensible or reasonable
examples: It makes sense to wait until a sunny day to visit the park together.
That Jimmy ran away from home suddenly doesn't make sense to any of us.

meaningEn: to depart quickly (also: to storm out); to act suddenly For the second definition, this idiom is usually followed by a gerund form such as laughing, crying, singing, etc.
examples: Faye and Debbie were so angry at each other that one of them burst out the front door of the house and the other stormed out the back door.
It was so funny to see a little baby in the audience burst out crying when the choir group burst out singing at the start of the recital.

meaningEn: to get free, to escape
examples: We always try to get away from the noise and heat of the city for a month or two each summer.
No one knows how the suspected criminal got away from the police.

meaningEn: to avoid punishment for
examples: Jonathan tries to get away with coming late to work almost every day; someday he'll suffer the consequences.
Terence can't continue to put his friends down like that and expect to get away with it forever.

meaningEn: to receive one's just punishment (S) This idiom is usually used at the beginning of a sentence after the subject it. Compare the following examples with those in the previous idiom above.
examples: It serves Jonathan right to be fired from his job.
It serves Terence right that none of his friends are willing to help him move to a new apartment.

meaningEn: to prevent from sleeping (S); to continue maintaining (speed, level of work, condition, etc.) (S)
examples: Could you please turn down the TV volume? You're keeping up the children.
If we can keep up this speed, we should arrive there in about two hours.
James is so proud of his daughter for getting mostly A's in school. He's certain that she can keep up the good work.

meaningEn: to have current knowledge of; to understand as an explanation This idiom should be compared to the meaning of to keep up with in Lesson 17.
examples: Evan keeps up with world affairs by reading a new magazine each week.
I understand a lot of the Spanish language, but I can't keep up with the fast conversation in this Mexican film.

meaningEn: to be easily visible or noticeable (also: to stick out) This idiom is used for someone or something that is different from all others.
examples: Her bright red hair makes her stand out from others in the group.
Brandon Styles is a tall, distinguished gentleman who sticks out in any crowd.

meaningEn: to reveal or tell what you know, to hint
examples: We are going to the movies tonight and we don't want Doris to go. If you see her, make sure not to let on.
They asked me not to let on to Ted that we're planning the birthday party; it's supposed to be a big surprise.

meaningEn: to fail, to result badly
examples: Something went wrong with the engine, so we had to have the car towed to a garage.
Shawn should have been here over an hour ago; I'm certain that something went wrong.

meaningEn: to compromise with someone
examples: Steve wanted $4,500 for his car, and Gwen offered $4,000. They met each other halfway and agreed on $4,250.
After a long process of give and take, the owners of the company agreed to meet the workers halfway by providing some additional health benefits but no wage increase.

meaningEn: to examine with the purpose of determining condition (also: to check on) This idiom has the related noun form checkup.
examples: The government always checks up on the background of employees who are hired for sensitive military projects.
The doctor wants me to have a thorough medical checkup as part of a preventive medicine program.

meaningEn: to point or place upwards (S); to rob (S)
examples: You should put some water on your hair. It's sticking up in the back.
A masked thief stuck up a grocery store in the neighborhood last night.

meaningEn: to happen
examples: I didn't find any explanation in the newspaper about how the political coup came about.
The flood came about as a result of the heavy winter rains.

meaningEn: to cause to happen This idiom is used to indicate who or what caused something to come about.
examples: John brought about the accident because of his carelessness.
The heavy rains we have each spring bring about serious flooding.

meaningEn: to increase slowly, to make stronger gradually (S)
examples: They built up their savings account so that they could buy a new house.
The professional athlete exercises regularly to build her strength up.

meaningEn: to decrease, to lessen in strength
examples: The hurricane became a less serious tropical storm when its winds died down.
We let the fire in the fireplace die down and enjoyed watching the embers as they glowed in the dark.

meaningEn: to diminish gradually in time or distance
examples: The memory of that unpleasant experience has slowly faded away.
The music of the band gradually faded away as the parade passed down the street.

meaningEn: not to exist anymore; to be in the process of disappearing
examples: Scientists still are not sure exactly why the dinosaurs died out.
That strange, new style of dancing is slowly dying out.

examples: The letter was so poorly handwritten that I couldn't make out many of the words.
Harold, please make the check out to Acme Piano Company.

meaningEn: to fulfill (a standard or promise)
examples: It was clear that the lazy student would never live up to his family's expectations.
It surprised us that the car salesperson lived up to all the promises he made.

meaningEn: to adhere to (a promise), to follow or obey (a set of rules, procedures, etc.)
examples: He made a promise to his wife to quit smoking and drinking, and so far he has stuck to it.
All organizations expect their employees to stick to established work rules and procedures.
If you try hard to stick to your principles, then you'll be able to live up to them.

meaningEn: to cheat, to take unfair advantage of (also: to rip off, the ripoff)
examples: Be careful in doing business with that salesperson. He'll stick it to you at the first opportunity.

You paid over $400 for that jacket? What a ripoff!

meaningEn: to insist on, to demand; to defend, to support
examples: If you don't stand up for your rights in court, the lawyers will try to stick it to you.
Frank stood up for his friend, who was being put down by other teenagers nearby.

meaningEn: to economize, to save money
examples: Most students live on limited budgets and have to cut corners whenever possible.
The Livingstons have nine children, so it is essential that they cut corners at all times.

meaningEn: to employ, to hire (S); to accept responsibility for, to undertake
examples: That factory is taking a lot of new employees on for its new production line.
Would you be willing to take on the task of organizing the next company picnic?

meaningEn: to remove from an elevated place (S); to write what is said, to note
examples: We should take the pictures down from the wall and clean off the dust.
The secretary took down everything that was said at the meeting.

meaningEn: to fail to materialize, not to succeed This idiom is usually used with the noun plan or plans as the subject.
examples: Our plan to travel to Europe last summer fell through when we were unable to save up enough money.
Felix made plans to have a party for everyone in his office, but they fell through at the last moment.

meaningEn: to surrender, to stop resisting
examples: Completely surrounded by our soldiers, the enemy finally gave in.
Management gave in to the strikers' demands and agreed to a shortened work week.

meaningEn: to release, to produce, to release
examples: When water boils, it gives off stream.
The flowers in this garden give off a strange odor.

meaningEn: to distribute; to become exhausted or depleted (also: to run out) The first definition has the same meaning as the second definition of to pass out in Lesson 19.
examples: An usher stood at the door of the theater giving out programs.
I couldn't finish the ten-mile race because my energy gave out.
Jeff plans to stay in Las Vegas and gamble until his money runs out.

meaningEn: to want revenge on, to feel hostile towards (also: to hold a grudge against)
examples: Martina expects to lose her job because her boss has had it in for her for a long time.
The teacher has held a grudge against Al ever since the time that he insulted her in front of the class.

meaningEn: to quarrel with, to confront
examples: I am going to have it out with Jack about all the times that he has told us lies.
Ben had it out with his roommate about coming back home so late and making a lot of noise.

meaningEn: to delay, or to be delayed, in occurring (S) This idiom has the same meaning as to put off in Lesson 5 when a noun or pronoun is used as an object, as in the second example.
examples: If the rain holds off for a few more days, they can finish planting the rest of the crop.
The judge agreed to hold off making a decision until new evidence could be introduced into court.

meaningEn: to endure, to be sufficient; to survive by resisting; to persist in one's efforts The first definition for to hold out has the opposite meaning of the second definition for to give out (seventh idiom, this lesson).
examples: If our supply of food and water holds out, we plan to camp here for another week. However, whenever it gives out, we'll have to leave.
That nation's troops cannot hold out much longer against the superior forces of the enemy.
The valuable football player held out for more money before signing a new contract with his team.

meaningEn: to extend, to keep for a longer time (S)

I have to take this book back to the library today.

examples: He is, on the whole, a good student.

The advertising department worked out a plan to increase company sales.

Wait a minute. Could you back up and say that again?

meaningEn: to drive a vehicle out of a parking space (S); to withdraw support, to fail to fulfill a promise or obligation

meaningEn: to become popular or widespread; to understand, to appreciate a joke This idiom is often used with the preposition to for the second definition.
examples: Fashions of the past often catch on again among young people.

examples: Instead of throwing out our paper waste in the office, we should recycle it.
When a fight broke out between two people on the dance floor, the management threw them out.
The judge threw the case out because there was insufficient evidence to try the defendant successfully.

meaningEn: to erect or construct quickly (S); to vomit (S)

examples: The teacher tried to clear up our confusion about the meaning of the difficult paragraph in the reading.

meaningEn: to go, or cause to go, more slowly (also: to slow up) (S) This idiom can be used both with and without an object.
examples: The car was going so fast that the motorist couldn't slow it down enough to make the sharp curve.

Slow up a bit! You're talking so quickly that I can't catch on well.

meaningEn: to lose, or cause to lose, all moisture (S); to be depleted

meaningEn: to be doing something; to be planning or plotting something, scheming The first definition usually takes the form of a question.
examples: Hi, Jake. I haven't seen you in a long time. What have you been up to?
Those boys hiding behind the building must be up to something bad.

meaningEn: to avoid discussing directly, to evade the issue
examples: Our boss beats around the bush so much that no one in the office knows exactly what he wants us to do.
Instead of beating around the bush, Melinda explained her objection in very clear terms.

examples: The meeting finally came to an end at ten o'clock in the evening.

meaningEn: to cause to end, to terminate in a definite manner (also: to do away with)

meaningEn: to waste time (also: to screw around); to joke, not to be serious
examples: The teacher got angry because her students were fooling around and couldn't finish their work before the end of class.
